teams.heading: Fiji languish at bottom of Nations Championship table after Scotland defeat
teams.body: Fiji sit in 12th place out of 12 teams in the Nations Championship table. The Flying Fijians have suffered three defeats in their opening three tournament matches. They scored 49 points across those three fixtures. The defence conceded 145 points over the same matches. That leaves the team with a tournament points difference of -96. Their last outing resulted in a 17-33 defeat against Scotland in Round 3. It is a stark contrast to 2023, when the team reached their highest world ranking of No. 7.

teams.heading: Zoe Harrison seals England Women victory over New Zealand with overtime try
teams.body: Fly-half Zoe Harrison intercepted a pass in the 81st minute to secure a 26-19 victory for England Women over New Zealand at Allianz Stadium. Playing in front of a crowd of 59,871, the Red Roses bounced back from last weekend's draw with Canada. Tries from Claudia Moloney-MacDonald, Ellie Kildunne and Jess Breach kept John Mitchell's side in contention before Harrison's late intervention settled the contest. The result extends England's unbeaten run to 41 Tests ahead of their trip to Canada.

teams.body: France currently sit third in the 12-nation standings following the conclusion of the opening three rounds of the Nations Championship. teams.heading: Ireland women make six changes for Sunday fixture against Japan
teams.body: Ireland head coach Scott Bemand has reshuffled his side for today's WXV Global Series encounter against Japan in Galway. Following last weekend’s defeat to the USA, Bemand has introduced Béibhinn Parsons, Anna McGann, and Aoibheann Reilly to the backline, while Eilís Cahill, Neve Jones, and Brittany Hogan join the starting pack. Aoife Wafer is ruled out due to a minor training injury. Bemand noted the matches against Japan and South Africa provide an opportunity to develop attacking prowess and technical cohesion.

teams.heading: Uruguayan Flanker Lucas Bianchi Completes Move To Italian Club Viadana
teams.body: Uruguayan international Lucas Bianchi has joined Serie A Elite side Viadana. The 25-year-old flanker, who represented Los Teros at the 2023 Rugby World Cup, moves to Italy following a stint as a key member of the leadership team at Peñarol. Bianchi is one of several Uruguayan players securing contracts in Europe ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup cycle, bolstering the Viadana pack for the upcoming season in Italy’s premier domestic division.

teams.heading: Scotland Women Suffer Defeat After Overturning Lead Against Australia side
teams.body: Scotland Women were unable to secure a victory in their final WXV Global Series fixture, falling to a defeat against Australia. Despite establishing a first-half lead, the side was undone by ill-discipline as the visitors successfully overturned the deficit. This result concludes a challenging tournament for the Scots, who had previously faced heavy losses against Canada and New Zealand earlier in the series, though they did manage to accumulate 40 points across their opening two encounters.

teams.heading: Wales women suffer narrow defeat against USA at Cardiff Arms Park
teams.body: Wales women’s resurgence suffered a blow on Saturday as they were edged 24-26 by a clinical USA side in their WXV Global Series contest. Despite tries from Keira Bevan, Kelsey Jones, Sisilia Tuipulotu and Alex Callender, the hosts were unable to contain USA number eight Freda Tafuna, who secured a decisive hat-trick. The visitors dominated the second half, leaving Wales to refocus before their upcoming fixture in Japan next month. This result halts momentum following last week’s impressive win over South Africa.

teams.heading: French court sentences two men for murder of Federico Martín Aramburú
teams.body: A Paris court has concluded the trial regarding the 2022 death of former Argentina international Federico Martín Aramburú. Loik Le Priol was sentenced to 26 years in prison for the murder, while Romain Bouvier received 19 years for attempted murder. The court found that the two men, both former members of a far-right group, acted with a shared focus on violence. Aramburu, who earned 22 caps for Los Pumas, was killed following an altercation at a cafe in Paris.

teams.heading: New Zealand women lose to England following late Zoe Harrison try
teams.body: The Black Ferns suffered a heart-breaking 26-19 defeat against England at Allianz Stadium on Saturday. Despite leading 12-7 at half-time through tries from Amy Du Plessis and Ayesha Leti-I'iga, New Zealand fell away as England capitalised on a second-half yellow card for Veisinia Mahutariki-Fakalelu. The scores were level at 19-19 late in the contest before Zoe Harrison’s interception try in added time ended New Zealand's eight-match winning streak. Captain Georgia Ponsonby highlighted the intensity of the encounter between the world's top two sides.
